title: Merit List Swaps

examples.explanation: The out-of-order pairs are (3, 1), (3, 2) and (5, 4). Each swap of two neighbours fixes exactly one of them.
Equal scores are already in order.

hints: A swap of two neighbours changes the relative order of exactly one pair. So the answer is the number of pairs i < j with aᵢ > aⱼ: the inversions.
Counting inversions pair by pair is O(n²). Merge sort can count them while it merges: when an element from the right half is placed first, it jumps over every element still waiting in the left half.
Another way: scan right to left and keep a Fenwick tree of the values seen so far (after compressing them to 1..n). For each aᵢ, count how many seen values are smaller.
